## ✨ Highlights

- 🗺️ **Traffic flow**: a node's page in the Controller now draws its HAProxy live - the node's interfaces, HAProxy, each frontend, the backends it sends to and their servers - with the traffic, sessions and state of each, and links that pulse where traffic goes. The whole map in your window, as big as it allows - a seventeen-backend load balancer fits a 1920x1080 screen.
- 💻 **The same map in your terminal**: `f` in `janusctl tui` draws a node's traffic flow with box-drawing lines that run where traffic goes, a cursor to follow it, and a server's Ready / Drain / Maint at Enter - laid out to fit the terminal it's in.
- 📊 **A Grafana dashboard** for the Janus exporter, held to what janusd actually exports, and alert rules that say what fired and where.
- ⚡ **Updates and reboots through kexec, from the Controller and Terraform**: a node's Update and Power pages, and `janus_node`'s new `update_reboot_mode`, reboot a node straight into its new kernel, without the firmware - seconds where a server's POST takes a minute.

## 🗺️ Traffic flow

- **Monitoring › Traffic flow** on a node's page: interfaces → HAProxy → frontends → backends → servers, drawn from what HAProxy counts (`show stat`, at the page's refresh interval) and from its configuration.
- **The whole map, as big as the window allows**: by default (**Auto**) the map is drawn whole in the window - width and height -, from 75 % up to 150 % of its size, so a big screen shows it bigger; the page uses the full width of the screen for it. Of its three shapes - left to right with the labels under the nodes, left to right with the labels beside them (rows half as tall, for many backends), top to bottom - it takes the one that shows the map the biggest, and follows the window as it's resized. A map too big to be whole at 75 % is drawn as wide as the page, which scrolls down it. **Vertical** and **Horizontal** in the page's header force a direction, and the browser remembers the choice. The details go beside the map when that leaves it room enough, below it otherwise - and then a selected node's details stay pinned at the bottom of the window. The map never moves as the numbers change.
- **Where traffic can go** comes from the configuration: `default_backend` (a `defaults` section's too), `use_backend` with its condition, a `listen` section's own servers - and a `use_backend %[...]` that reads a map, directly or through a `set-var`: the map's values are the backends, and its keys say for what (a host-to-backend map shows each backend with its host names). A `use_backend` nothing on the node can resolve is said in the frontend's details, not guessed.
- **Live**: each node shows its traffic and sessions, or what's wrong with it - a backend with servers down, a server failing its checks (`DOWN · L4TOUT`), in maintenance or draining; links pulse where bytes flow, thicker and faster the more there are (still, for whoever asked their system for less motion). HAProxy doesn't count how a backend's traffic splits between the frontends that send to it: the numbers are the proxies' own.
- **Details**: hover a node to bring its paths forward; select a frontend for its counters and the rules behind each of its links, a backend for what reaches it, a server for its check, address and timings - and **Ready / Drain / Maint**, as on HAProxy › Backends. The **Servers** chip folds the servers away on a big configuration (past eight per backend, "+N more").
- **Rights**: what an account may read on the node, as everywhere on the page. An account whose grant leaves out HAProxy's domain sees the frontends, backends and servers without the links between them (the configuration and the maps aren't read for it), and the page says so.
- Works with nodes of every version: it reads what nodes already serve.

## ⚡ kexec from the Controller and Terraform

`janusctl` has had `-kexec` since v2026.10.10; the Controller and the Terraform provider now have it too.

- **A node's Update page**: **Reboot through kexec**, with each of the three ways an update reaches the node (the node downloads it, the Controller pushes it, files uploaded from the browser). The page then says how the node reboots: "through kexec, without the firmware", or through the firmware and why.
- **A node's Power page**: **Through kexec** on the Reboot card.
- **Terraform**: `update_reboot_mode = "kexec"` on a `janus_node` - its updates of version, extensions, HAProxy branch or kernel track reboot through kexec. Set together with a new `version`, that update already does. The default stays `"firmware"`, and the machine's history on the Controller says which way each update went. The Controller's API takes the same `update_reboot_mode` on `/api/machines`.
- The rules are `janusctl`'s: opt-in, unchecked each time; with Secure Boot on, only an image signed by Janus can be kexec'd - an update then reboots through the firmware and says so, a reboot is refused with nothing rebooted; a revert always goes through the firmware. Nodes from v2026.10.10 on; an older node reboots through the firmware.
- On a phone, the Update page's checkboxes no longer shrink to a dot.

## 🔄 The Controller

- **Refresh** in the Controller's header now also asks GitHub for its releases again: a release or pre-release published a moment ago shows at once, instead of within ten minutes. **Refresh now** on a node's page does the same for that node's update check. At most once every 30 seconds; if GitHub doesn't answer then, the list in hand stays.

## 💻 janusctl

- **`janusctl tui`: `f` on a node** draws its traffic flow in the terminal, as the Controller does: the interfaces, HAProxy, the frontends, the backends they send to and their servers, with each one's traffic and sessions. A link carrying traffic runs, a link to a server down is dashed red, one in maintenance dotted, a backend no rule names is a hollow ○.
- **It fits the terminal**: left to right when it fits, else top to bottom when that does, else the way that hides less of it, its nodes closer together when that's what makes it fit; the details beside it narrow down, or go below it, to leave it room, and a resize lays it out again. A seventeen-backend edge load balancer fits a 160x48 terminal whole. Each label keeps room for its numbers: the map holds still as traffic comes and goes.
- **`o`** shows the other way and, pressed again, goes back to auto; **`s`** hides the servers. The arrows move a cursor along the map - with the flow to follow the traffic, across to go along a level -: the paths through the node under it come forward, and its counters, a frontend's binds and the rules behind its links (a map's keys included) show beside the map, or below it on a terminal under 150 columns. **Enter** on a server sets it ready, drain or maint, as from the servers' table; `f` or Esc goes back.
- The **M** menu remembers the flow's direction (auto, or one way for good), its servers and whether its links run (`tui.json`). On the Linux console, whose font lacks them, the heavy and dashed lines are drawn with what it has.
- A certificate whose role may not read HAProxy's configuration gets the proxies without the links between them, and the map says why. Works with nodes of every version.

## 📊 Monitoring

- **`grafana/janus-nodes.json`**: the nodes a Prometheus job scrapes, all or some - an overview, a line per node (release, schematic, HAProxy and kernel, slot, boot, NTP, SELinux), HAProxy serving with its reloads, crashes and configurations, certificates by expiry and Let's Encrypt's, extension services, trials, the clock, API calls and errors, and a folded row for VRRP, BGP and the firewall's sets; janusd starting, configurations applied and HAProxy crashing as annotations. Built and checked against janusd's own metrics; tried on Grafana 11.6, 12.0 and 13.0 ([Grafana dashboard](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/metrics.md#grafana-dashboard)).
- **Alerts** (`examples/prometheus/janus-rules.yml`): every rule now has a summary (what, and on which instance) and a description (the certificate, service, VRRP instance or BGP neighbor concerned). Expressions, delays and severities are unchanged.

## 🔧 Tests and docs

- Each pre-release's lab campaign is recorded in the repository (`docs/pre-release-tests/`): CI, rolling update under load, failovers, reboots, rollback and HAProxy's throughput, compared with the previous release.
- The node page and `janusctl tui` read configurations the same way - one in the browser, one in Go - and are held to the same test cases.
- The Controller's self-update test no longer fails on a long log (a false negative in v2026.10.12's first run).

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Nodes**: the usual A/B update. Nothing changes on a node in this release.
- **The Controller**: update it from its update card - Traffic flow, the kexec choices and Refresh are the Controller's.
- **janusctl**: `apt update && apt install janusctl`, or the release's `.deb` - `f` in `janusctl tui`.
- **The Terraform provider**: this release's provider, for `update_reboot_mode` on `janus_node`. A configuration that doesn't set it plans no change.
